US Intelligence Captures Clear Imagery of Secretive Chinese Spaceplane

Visual Confirmation in Orbit

Newly released images from the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) have provided the first high-resolution look at China’s secretive, reusable spaceplane. Captured by a commercial Maxar satellite, the photo reveals a design bearing striking similarities to the US Space Force’s X-37B, including delta wings and a rear-mounted service module.

Capability and Context

The Chinese vehicle, often referred to as CSSHQ, operates in low-Earth orbit and has demonstrated maneuvers such as deploying and recapturing sub-satellites. While its exact mission remains classified, the DIA notes that its enhanced maneuverability makes it ideal for specialized space operations. This imagery highlights the growth of non-Earth imaging (NEI), where commercial satellites track orbital objects. Further details on the threat assessment regarding China's directed-energy weapons and counterspace technology can be found in the official report: https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/10/chinas-top-secret-spaceplane-cant-hide-in-low-earth-orbit/.
